comparison: Both evaluations strongly support the burst-pause response findings (C6, C7, C43-C52, C56-C57). OpenEval emphasizes dose-dependent relationships and appropriate controls, while peer reviewers describe the evidence as 'convincing' and 'robust and reliable.' High agreement with 13/14 claims overlapping.

Both support Kv1 channel involvement in pause response. OpenEval covers broader claim set (C7, C58-C65, C70, C128, C146, C171) emphasizing pharmacological rigor, while peer review focuses on subset (C60-C62, C70, C128, C146, C171). Peer reviewers found evidence 'convincing' and 'robust.'

Both support negative control findings excluding other potassium channels (C66-C69, C124-C126). OpenEval explicitly evaluates these controls, while peer review implicitly accepts them through endorsement of main Kv1 findings. 3/7 claims directly overlap.

OpenEval R4 addresses D2R modulation (C8, C71-C74, C80, C82, C143, C166) while peer R5 addresses same claims. Both support findings with 5/9 claims overlapping. OpenEval notes modest effects appropriately acknowledged; peer reviewers accept D2R modulatory role as part of D2R/D5R balance.

OpenEval R5 evaluates D5R inhibition of pause (C9, C75-C79, C88-C89, C144-C145, C147) while peer R4 addresses overlapping D5R claims. Both strongly support findings with 9/11 claims overlapping. Peer reviewers found D5R-cAMP-Kv1 signaling 'convincing' and experiments properly designed.

Perfect agreement on Ih not being required for pause initiation (C84-C87, C121-C123). Both evaluations support these findings that refute prior theories. All 7 claims overlap completely (Jaccard=1.0).

Both support dyskinetic mouse model characterization and loss of pause response (C93-C101, C154). OpenEval emphasizes model validation and consistency with prior Kv1 work, while peer reviewers note it bridges previous CIN hyperexcitability findings. 9/13 claims overlap.

Both support negative findings that D2R stimulation fails to restore pause in dyskinetic mice (C102-C106, C168-C169). OpenEval emphasizes this as important negative finding; peer reviewers accepted data despite surprising result. 7/8 claims overlap.

Both strongly support clozapine restoration of pause through D5R inverse agonism. OpenEval covers broader claim set (C11-C12, C107-C120, C155-C158, C161-C163, C172, C174) emphasizing pharmacological rigor, while peer review focuses on subset (C11, C114, C116-C120, C158, C161-C162). 10/25 claims directly overlap.

Partial overlap on clozapine mechanism and D5R-cAMP-Kv1 signaling pathway. OpenEval R9 addresses clozapine experiments while peer R11 emphasizes the mechanistic model (C107-C111, C155-C156, C163, C173-C174). Both support findings with 9/25 claims overlapping.

Both address D5R constitutive activity mechanism for Kv1 suppression. OpenEval R10 focuses on integration with prior work (C16, C155-C156, C163-C165), while peer R11 emphasizes D5R-cAMP-Kv1 signaling model. 3/6 claims overlap; both acknowledge need for further mechanistic validation.

OpenEval R11 addresses thalamic input dynamics (C53-C55, C131-C133) while peer R14 covers broader interpretive claims. Limited overlap (3/6 claims) but both support integration of findings with broader context.
OpenEval R12 addresses single-spike pause and ex vivo model validation (C134-C138) while peer R14 covers broader discussion claims. 5/5 claims overlap; both support these findings without challenge.
OpenEval R13 summarizes recent in vivo findings from other groups (C139-C142) while peer R14 addresses broader interpretive context. 4/4 claims overlap; both accept these contextual citations.

OpenEval R14 rates speculative claims as UNCERTAIN (C148-C152) while peer R12 supports physiological interpretation (C148). Divergence: OpenEval views these as untested hypotheses, peer reviewers accept physiological relevance interpretation. Only 1/5 claims overlap.

OpenEval rates speculative/interpretive claims as UNCERTAIN (C148-C152) while peer R14 supports broader discussion claims including some overlap (C149-C152). 4/5 claims overlap but evaluation types differ: OpenEval=UNCERTAIN vs Peer=SUPPORTED.

Both support background and contextual claims establishing study rationale. OpenEval R15 covers extensive background (C1-C5, C17-C42, C45, C90-C92, C159-C160, C170, C173) while peer R13 addresses overlapping background claims. 34/38 claims overlap; both note these provide established context rather than novel findings.

OpenEval R16 addresses inferences about DA concentrations in slice (C83, C167) while peer R14 covers broader interpretive claims. Minimal overlap (1/2 claims); both support these inferences as reasonable given experimental context.

Peer R10 addresses control finding that clozapine effects are independent of serotonin receptors (C115, C160). No corresponding OpenEval result specifically evaluates this control, though OpenEval R9 includes C115 in broader clozapine mechanism evaluation.
